Importunate describes a person (or their behavior) who keeps demanding or asking for something in a persistent, annoying, and pressure-filled way — and who simply refuses to stop or take no for an answer, even when it is clearly unwelcome.

Think about the most relentless, pestering person you can imagine. Not someone who asks once. Not someone who asks twice and then politely lets it go. But someone who keeps pushing, keeps pressing, keeps demanding — again and again — with an urgency that makes you feel cornered and uncomfortable.

That person is importunate.

The word carries three things at once:

  1. Persistence — they do not stop asking.
  2. Urgency or pressure — they ask in a way that feels forceful, not gentle.
  3. Disregard — they ignore your discomfort, your refusal, or the fact that their timing is inconvenient or inappropriate.

It is not just stubbornness. An importunate person actively presses on despite clear signals that they should stop. This is what makes it feel so wearing and intrusive to the person on the receiving end.

Imagine a door-to-door salesman who you've told "No, thank you" — but he keeps talking, steps closer, brings up new arguments, follows up with calls, and simply will not let the matter rest. You feel trapped and exhausted. That feeling — that draining, suffocating sense of being relentlessly pressured — is precisely what importunate behavior produces.

It is different from someone being enthusiastic or eager. Those are positive or neutral qualities. Importunate has a negative charge — it is always used to signal that the behavior has crossed a line into something troubling or burdensome.

• The importunate beggar followed the tourists down three streets, tugging at their sleeves and pleading without pause.
  • She found his importunate requests for money deeply exhausting; no matter how many times she said no, he always came back asking again.
  • The minister grew tired of the importunate petitioners who crowded his door every morning with endless demands.
  • His importunate behavior at the meeting — constantly interrupting, pushing his agenda, refusing to yield the floor — made everyone uncomfortable.

Notice how in every case, the behavior is unwanted, relentless, and socially inappropriate in its forcefulness.
How It Differs from Similar Words

These words are related but not identical:

  • Persistent is neutral — a persistent person keeps trying, and this can even be admirable (a persistent athlete, a persistent student). Importunate is never admirable.
  • Pushy is informal and mild. Importunate is more formal and more severe — it suggests a deeper, more exhausting kind of pressure.
  • Nagging usually refers to repeated complaints or reminders, often within close relationships. Importunate is broader and stronger — it implies forceful demands, not just repetitive complaints.
  • Insistent just means someone firmly maintains a position. Importunate adds the layer of harassment — of wearing someone down with demands.

The key distinction of importunate is that it combines persistence with pressure with social intrusiveness, all in one word.
It Can Describe People or Things

While it most commonly describes a person's behavior, it can also describe the demands or requests themselves:

  • He faced importunate demands from his creditors every single week.
  • The letter contained an importunate plea that she found impossible to ignore.

Here, the requests themselves are described as pressing, relentless, and difficult to brush aside.
The Register and Tone of the Word

Importunate is a formal, literary word. You are more likely to encounter it in classic novels, formal essays, journalism, or careful writing than in everyday conversation. When you see it, you know the writer is deliberately emphasizing how aggressively and relentlessly the person in question pressed their demands — it is never an accidental or casual choice of word.
A Simple Way to Remember It

If you ever want to recall this word quickly, think: "Import + unable to shut the door on." An importunate person imports themselves into your space and your life, uninvited, over and over, and you simply cannot get them to leave or stop. They are the person who will not be turned away.

Importunate = annoyingly and relentlessly persistent in making demands or requests, in a way that is forceful, intrusive, and completely indifferent to refusal or discomfort. It is a formal word with a strong negative meaning, used to describe people or behavior that exhausts and pressures others by simply never letting up.
